name: New Year's Eve
h1: New Year's Eve Charcuterie Board Ideas
seo_title: New Year's Eve Charcuterie Board Ideas + Midnight Plan
description: New Year's Eve charcuterie board ideas: a Champagne board, a midnight clock board, a caviar-and-chips splurge, a refill plan that lasts until midnight, and how much to buy.
answer: A New Year's Eve board has to last until midnight, so plan it as the party food (about 3 oz each of cheese and meat per guest), pair it with Champagne or Prosecco, and keep half the food in the fridge for a second round around 10 pm. Salty, crisp things (Parmigiano, potato chips, salami) and one splurge like smoked salmon or caviar make it feel like a celebration.

ideas.title: The Champagne Board
ideas.text: Built for bubbles: chunks of Parmigiano-Reggiano, a triple-crème, prosciutto, Marcona almonds, kettle chips, gougères and strawberries. Salt and fat are what make Champagne taste its best.

ideas.title: The Caviar and Chips Splurge
ideas.text: Kettle chips with crème fraîche and a tin of caviar or trout roe, blini, smoked salmon, chives and a good Comté, with a bottle of brut. Small portions, big effect.

ideas.title: The Midnight Refill Tray
ideas.text: Build one board for the start of the party and keep a second tray ready in the fridge: more cheese, salami, crackers and grapes, plus something warm like sliders for the 10 pm slump.

shapes.name: Midnight Clock Board
steps: On a round board, set a small bowl of jam or honey in the center.
Place 12 cheese cubes or cracker stacks around the edge as the hours.
Make the hands from two breadsticks or folded prosciutto, both pointing at 12.

shapes.name: Confetti Stripe Board
steps: On a rectangle, lay diagonal stripes of gold, white and dark: Gouda, Brie, salami, then repeat.
Fill the gaps between stripes with crackers and Marcona almonds.
Scatter pomegranate seeds or edible gold sprinkles over the top just before serving.

plan.what: Buy crackers, chips, nuts, jams and the sparkling wine.
Buy cheese, meat and fruit. Put the wine in the fridge.
Cut cheese, fold meats and pack the refill tray. Cover both and chill.
Take hard cheese out of the fridge and build the first board.
Swap in the refill tray. Anything perishable that has been out 2 hours goes back in the fridge or in the bin.

faq.q: What goes on a New Year's Eve charcuterie board?
faq.a: Salty, crisp and rich things that suit sparkling wine: Parmigiano-Reggiano, a triple-crème or Brie, prosciutto and salami, Marcona almonds, kettle chips, gougères and strawberries. Add one splurge, like smoked salmon or caviar, for midnight.

Salty, nutty and creamy cheeses: Parmigiano-Reggiano, aged Comté, Brie and triple-crème. The bubbles and acidity cut the fat, and the salt makes the wine taste fruitier. Strong blues tend to overpower a dry Champagne.

faq.q: How do I keep a charcuterie board fresh until midnight?
faq.a: Don't put everything out at once. Perishable food should sit out no more than 2 hours (1 hour above 90°F), so build a first board for the start of the party and keep a second tray in the fridge to swap in around 10 pm. Add crackers and chips last so they stay crisp.

faq.q: How much charcuterie do I need for a New Year's Eve party?
faq.a: If the board is the party food, plan about 3 oz each of cheese and meat per guest and 10 to 12 crackers; if there's dinner first, 2 oz of each is enough. From 20 guests, add 10%.

faq.q: What can I serve instead of expensive caviar?
faq.a: Trout or salmon roe gives the same salty pop for less. Serve it on kettle chips or blini with a spoon of crème fraîche or sour cream and chopped chives.
